sentences.text: The informant instituted the FIR at Police Station Majhola, District Moradabad stating that her husband had all of sudden disappeared in the year 2017.
The said missing report has been reported at Police Station Bajpur, District Udham Singh Nagar (Uttarakhand) by the informant as such he could not be traced to date.
The informant had two siblings.

5. After a period of about three years of the disappearance of the husband of the informant, she came in contact with the applicant, who called her to his house on some pretext and committed rape with her.
He informed that he was a widower and as such also stated that he shall marry her.
6. The informant entered into corporeal relationship with the applicant on the said promise of marriage.
The applicant kept on dilly-dallying with the said promise of marriage by adding vermilion to her forehead.
7. After about six months, it was revealed that the applicant was a married person and had siblings from his earlier married.

The informant decided to part ways with the applicant after getting the said information of marriage, but the said disassociation of the informant made him angry and he showed her an indecent video, whereby she was shown entering into physical relationship with him.

8. Despite her request to the applicant to delete the said video, he did not delete it and kept on threatening her that he shall make it viral on social media and sent it to her children also, as such the said relationship continued for a subsequent period of two years.
9. The applicant is stated to have come to the house of the informant and demanded a ransom of Rs.10 lakhs for deleting the said video.
On showing her inability to give such a heavy amount to the applicant, he is stated to have transferred certain call recordings and chats with the informant to her daughter and son.
The applicant is even stated to have threatened to put the two siblings to death.

10. The informant was terrified with the applicant as he is a person with criminal background and several cases are pending against him, as such the FIR was instituted at the police station on an application moved by the informant on 02.02.2024.

ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF APPLICANT:
11. The applicant is absolutely innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
12. The FIR is delayed by more than four years and there is no explanation of the said inordinate delay in the institution of the FIR.
13. The informant is a mature and married women aged about 44 years and she has three siblings from her earlier marriage i.e. two daughters and one son.
The daughter of the informant has instituted FIR No.948 of 2023, under Section 294 and 506 I.P.C. at Police Station Majhola, District Moradabad on 26.12.2023 making false allegations.
14. There are no allegations of rape against the applicant in the said FIR No.948 of 2023.

sentences.text: WhatsApp chats between the applicant and the informant herein were taken into possession by the investigating officer in Case Crime No.248 of 2023, which indicates her consent.
The said WhatsApp chats have been fled as Annexure No.4 to the affidavit accompanying the bail application.
In the said FIR No.948 of 2023, no allegations of sexual harassment have been made against the applicant.
The applicant has been enlarged on bail in the said case vide order dated 11.01.2024 by the Court of C.J.M., Moradabad.
16. The instant FIR has been instituted after the applicant was enlarged on bail in the said case.

The medical examination of the informant was conducted on 09.02.2024 and no alive or dead spermatozoa were seen in the vaginal smear of the victim, but in the supplementary medical report dated 13.03.2024 the doctor has opined 'As per above report and physical finding sexual violence cannot be ruled out'.
The said finding is without any evidence and cannot be taken into consideration.
17. The statements of the informant recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. and her two siblings do not corroborate the prosecution story.
There are ample contradictions in their statements.
18. The site plan has been prepared without help of the informant as such it has no value.
The informant was very much aware of the marital status of the applicant, which is but evident from the conversation and the photographs handed over by the informant.
19. It is an admitted fact that the informant was in corporeal relationship with the applicant for about three years but she did not report the matter during the said period.
The offence does not fall within the category of rape.

The offence, if any, may fall within the definition of Section 497 I.P.C.,
which stands deleted and was bailable.
20. The investigating officer has colluded with the informant and submitted the final report (charge-sheet) against the applicant.
21. If the allegations made in the FIR are to be believed, then also no offence of rape is made out against the applicant.
The offence made out, if any, may fall within the category of Section 406 I.P.C., which is the criminal breach of trust for the sake of arguments.
22. The Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
23. The applicant is languishing in jail since 13.04.2024 and is ready to cooperate with trial.

In case,
the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.

The criminal history assigned to the applicant stands explained as follows:
"(i) Case Crime No.0086/2024, under Sections 376, 384, 506 I.P.C. and 67A Information & Technology (Amendment) Act, 2008, Police Station Majhola, Distt- Moradabad.
--Present case.

ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF INFORMANT:
27.

The bail application has been opposed on the ground that in FIR No.948 of 2023, the victim has categorically stated that the applicant had harassed them and used to send indecent messages to them that too to the victim and her brother and other relatives in the family.
28. The informant herein had no knowledge about the marital status of the applicant and he had established corporeal relationship with her by deceiving her on the false promise of marriage.
29. The applicant has criminal history of ten cases assigned to him, as such on the basis of criminal antecedents he is not entitled for bail.

30. Much reliance has been placed on the judgment of Supreme Court passed in Anil Kumar Tulsiyani vs. State of U.P. & Another, (2006) 9 SCC 425, whereby the bail of the practicing advocate of this High Court was rejected by the Supreme Court on the ground that the High Court had not at all considered the gravity and nature of offence, for which the said offence has been considered that too to the murder of a close friend of the accused therein and that too in his bedroom.

sentences.text: ?The well-known principle of "Presumption of Innocence Unless Proven Guilty," gives rise to the concept of bail as a rule and imprisonment as an exception.

34. ?A person's right to life and liberty, guaranteed by Article 21 of the Indian Constitution, cannot be taken away simply because the person is accused of committing an offence until the guilt is established beyond a reasonable doubt.

Article 21 of the Indian Constitution states that no one's life or personal liberty may be taken away unless the procedure established by law is followed, and the procedure must be just and reasonable.

The said principle has been recapitulated by the Supreme Court in Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690.
35.

sentences.text: ?Reiterating the aforesaid view the Supreme Court in the case of Manish Sisodia vs. Directorate of Enforcement, 2024 INSC 595 has again emphasised that the very well-settled principle of law that bail is not to be withheld as a punishment is not to be forgotten.

sentences.text:
It is high time that the Courts should recognize the principle that "bail is a rule and jail is an exception".
36.
?Learned A.G.A. could not bring forth any exceptional circumstances which would warrant denial of bail to the applicant.
37. ?It is settled principle of law that the object of bail is to secure the attendance of the accused at the trial.

No material particulars or circumstances suggestive of the applicant fleeing from justice or thwarting the course of justice or creating other troubles in the shape of repeating offences or intimidating witnesses and the like have been shown by learned A.G.A.
38.

The judgment relied by the counsel for the informant does not carry weight as it does not match the circumstances of the instant case as the said case was of murder that too was committed in the house of the accused person.
39. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record

, taking into consideration the fact that the criminal history of the applicant has been properly explained coupled with the fact that the victim and the applicant were known to each other for more than four years, and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail. The bail application is allowed.

40. Let the applicant-Sanjay Kumar Shankhdhar involved in aforementioned case crime number be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the Trial Court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.
